extracted.intended_audience: Imaging scientists (faculty) and institutional grant applicants preparing proposals for the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative 'Advancing Imaging Through Collaborative Projects' RFA
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit an application for CZI's two-year collaborative imaging projects RFA, meeting eligibility, format, content, budget, data-sharing, ethical, and licensing requirements described by CZI. The application must designate a Coordinating PI (faculty imaging scientist) and include Co-PIs, proposal narrative, budget, CVs, and letters of commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility of Applicant Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be submitted by domestic and foreign nonprofit organizations; including public and private institutions, such as colleges, universities, hospitals, laboratories, units of state and local government; and eligible agencies of the federal government. Grants are not permitted to individuals, only to organizations. For profit organizations are not eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Network Organizations (nonprofits that bring together imaging scientists) may directly submit applications. There may be more than one application submitted by each organization. CZI reserves the sole right to decide if an applicant and applicant organization meet the eligibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinating PI qualifications and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Coordinating PI must be an Imaging Scientist and must have a faculty appointment (research or tenure track) or equivalent at an accredited institution at the time of grant start. The Coordinating PI will act as the administrative contact between CZI and all PIs on the grant and submit the application on behalf of the team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imaging Scientists might be engineers, physicists, mathematicians, computer scientists, or biologists focused on imaging technology development or who work at imaging core facilities. The Coordinating PI must be affiliated with the institution submitting the application; grant funds will be awarded to that institution. A person may serve as Coordinating PI on only one application, but may serve as a Co-PI on other applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-Principal Investigator (Co-PI) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application must include at least one Co-PI and may include up to ten Co-PIs. A Co-PI can be at any career stage, does not need to be an Imaging Scientist, and must be employed at an eligible non-profit organization or eligible agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-PIs may serve as Co-PI on multiple applications. Do not include the Coordinating PI in the Co-PI count. Provide Co-PI name, title, degrees, ORCID (if available), email, career status, organization details, and tax ID where requested. Upload a signed letter from each Co-PI describing their role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project types / Categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds can be requested in one or more categories: Validation and dissemination of new imaging technologies; Building capacity; Training and education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions: Validation/dissemination involves testing/validating new systems or adoption at imaging cores. Building capacity includes frameworks (websites, coordinating organizations) and online platforms to exchange methods/tools. Training/education includes organizing courses, train-the-trainers, media for training, and developing teaching materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project duration and start date
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards will be two years (24 months) in duration with an expected start date of March 1, 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selected projects will be funded for two years; grantees work towards completion of a collaborative project and specify metrics for success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget request and scrutiny threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants will request an appropriate award amount for the project. Applications requesting more than $350,000 total costs (inclusive of 15 percent indirect costs) for the overall project period (two years) will be subjected to additional scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget should reflect actual needs; CZI will work with successful applicants to arrive at a mutually acceptable budget after review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect cost policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect costs are limited to up to 15 percent of direct costs. Indirect costs may not be assessed on capital equipment or subcontracts, but subcontractors may include up to 15 percent indirect costs of their direct costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indirect cost amounts should be included in the total budget requested in USD. Institutions should consult institutional policy on indirect costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed expense categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Supported expense categories include: salary for the Imaging Scientist or additional personnel; subcontracting for creative work or events; travel and lodging; expenses for development/hosting/management of online projects; parts and shipping required to adopt new technology; publicity and promotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use requested grant funds appropriately by category. Note special restrictions for international grantees regarding activities and travel to the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: International grantee fund-use restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: International grantees must use all grant funds exclusively for activities conducted outside the United States of America. Travel expenses to the United States (including round-trip tickets) should not be covered from the requested grant funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any attendance at CZI meetings in the U.S. will be covered by CZI separately from requested grant funds. Note: institutions outside the U.S. may not subcontract to U.S. institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with U.S. sanctions and export controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be compliant with the U.S. Treasury Department’s OFAC sanctions program, U.S. Department of Commerce export administration regulations, the FCPA, and other applicable laws and corresponding laws where the applicant is based. Prior to award, all applications will be reviewed for compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of required ongoing compliance, an applicant’s funding eligibility may need to be reassessed if laws/regulations change. Consult your home institution for eligibility. CZI may reassess eligibility at any time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission platform and required familiarity
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications must be completed and submitted through CZI’s online grants management portal (SurveyMonkey Apply). SMApply is configured to work best using the Google Chrome browser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarize yourself with the portal well in advance. Deadline extensions will not be granted. For technical assistance contact support@smapply.io or use the portal help request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application component requirements (tasks)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application consists of the following sections: Coordinating PI Details, Equal Opportunity and Diversity, Organization Details for Coordinating PI, Project Details, Project Proposal, Budget, CVs for Coordinating PI and Co-PIs, and Letters of Commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete all required fields in each task. Some tasks state 'all fields are required.' Follow guidance for the information to enter in each task (e.g., Coordinating PI details, organization contacts, tax ID).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal formatting and upload requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal PDF uploads must use font 11 point or larger and margins at least one-half inch on letter size pages. Proposal body maximum is 2,500 words (includes 250-word abstract). Figures optional limited to two pages (legends do not count toward word count).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References have no word/page limit. CVs max three pages each, U.S. letter-sized, 11 point or larger font and 0.5 inch margins. Letters of Commitment must be PDFs and may be combined. Any materials exceeding word/page limits or not following requirements will not be considered during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal content structure and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal Body (max 2,500 words, includes 250-word Abstract) must include: Abstract, Background, Project Goals, Significance, Project Plan (strategy, expected outcomes, deliverables, timeline), Project Metrics. Milestones (max 500 words) and Expected Impact (quantitative estimate; max 250 words) are entered in Project Details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose field: one-sentence summary limited to 200 characters. Use third-person voice for required fields. Figures optional and limited to two pages. References are unrestricted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project metrics requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees will specify metrics to evaluate the project's success. Ideally, the metrics will be quantitative (e.g., number of applications of a new imaging technology installed in a lab or imaging core, number of people attending a training course or using an online training resource).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example metrics: number of researchers using a new technology, number of participants for a training/workshop, number of attendees at a meeting. Include milestones and measurable outcomes in the Project Details and Proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for award decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of awardees will be based on: the quality of the proposal and the expertise and capacity of the group for addressing the proposed project; significance and potential impact of the project; and potential of the awardee to contribute to an increased adoption of imaging in biomedical sciences in their region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CZI will evaluate applications for scientific merit through independent expert review; final decisions are made by CZI staff with scientific advisors. There is no expectation of any specific number of awards; CZI may choose not to recommend funding any applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and decision process (no feedback guarantee)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications will be reviewed by independent experts and final decisions made by CZI staff in consultation with scientific advisors. CZI does not provide feedback on decisions for unfunded proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Earliest notification of decisions indicated in timeline, but subject to change. CZI reserves right to request budget changes upon award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing and repository expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any datasets curated or generated must be made as publicly available and easily accessible through an appropriate data repository as legally permissible, under an Open Definition conformant license. Ideally, datasets would not include PII; if they do, consent to sharing must be obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide metadata, documentation, and intended use cases under an Open Definition conformant license, preferably CC0 or CC BY/CC BY SA where attribution is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and preprint policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications related to funded work must be submitted to a preprint server (such as bioRxiv, medRxiv, arXiv, or appropriate repository) at or before the first submission to a journal. Experimental protocols must be made publicly available through a protocol sharing service (e.g., protocols.io).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific publications, preprints, and presentations resulting from the award should acknowledge support from this funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software sharing, licensing, and packaging requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: CZI requires sharing of software code developed by grantees generally to be made publicly available on GitHub (or similar). All new code must be released under a permissive open source license (MIT, BSD 2-Clause, BSD 3-Clause, or Apache v2.0). All pre-existing and derivative code must be licensed under the most permissive license possible given prior licensing terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis packages must be released through appropriate language-specific package managers (e.g., PyPi, Bioconductor, CRAN) with documentation, example data, and interactive demos (e.g., Jupyter notebooks). Use Docker or similar containers to ensure portability and reproducibility. Software should be archived for long-term digital preservation and citability when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reagent and resource sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources and reagents developed with funding must be available for rapid dissemination to the community, where possible in an accessible community repository (e.g., Addgene for plasmids, Jackson Labs for model system lines). This applies to cell lines, transgenic organisms, plasmids/clones, antibodies, and other reagents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make reagents available rapidly to enable reuse; list repositories and planned distribution in the proposal where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical conduct and human/animal subjects requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees must adopt procedures for the use of animals and for the ethical treatment of human subjects and tissue donors, including obtaining written informed consent. CZI regards NIH policies as a strong model for such procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify any exceptions to broad sharing or consent at time of application; such requests may affect application success. Investigators are encouraged to discuss challenging consent situations with CZI scientific staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Approval Form requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload a single PDF Institutional Approval Form reviewed and signed by an authorized person at the organization agreeing to institutional and investigator commitments on data, resource sharing, publication policies, and confirming ability to receive funding. The policies are non-negotiable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digital signatures permitted provided the document is not encrypted or password-protected. While CZI does not require sign-off by all partner institutions, applicants should follow their institutional requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting enforcement and non-compliance consequence
rubrics_metrics.description: The formatting and component requirements, including word and page limits indicated, will be enforced by the review team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any submitted materials that exceed the word and page limits or do not follow the requirements will not be considered during the application review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of submitted applications
rubrics_metrics.description: All submitted applications will be kept confidential, except as necessary for evaluation or to comply with laws; and except where applications are made public without CZI fault. Successfully funded proposals may be made publicly available and/or shared with other grantees. Unfunded proposals will remain confidential, though aggregate summaries may be made public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application materials will not be returned to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibitions and disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Meta employees (including subsidiaries) and employees of Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, LLC, are not permitted to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CZI reserves the right to determine eligibility. Applicants are encouraged to consult sciencegrants@chanzuckerberg.com with eligibility questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: CV and Letters of Commitment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload CVs in PDF for the Coordinating PI and each Co-PI (combined or separate PDFs). Maximum of three pages per CV. Upload a signed letter from each Co-PI describing their role and contribution; do not include a letter from the Coordinating PI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required CV fields: Name; Current Position Title; Education/Training; Positions and Scientific Appointments; Publications (provide total number and selected list of 10 citations); How many years managing imaging cores (if applicable). Letters/digital signatures permitted if not encrypted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application fields for Project Details (concise purpose, amounts, milestones)
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Details require specific short fields: Purpose (one sentence, max 200 characters), Abstract/Project Summary (max 250 words), Type of Project (select categories), Amount Requested (USD, whole numbers only), Milestones (list, max 500 words), Expected Impact (quantitative estimate, max 250 words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use third-person voice for designated fields. Project title limited to 60 characters. Amount Requested must match Budget Description and be inclusive of indirects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carryover and extension policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Unused research funds may be carried over to the following year, and requests for no-cost extensions will be considered at the end of the overall project period upon receipt of an annual report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees may obtain funds from other sources provided there is no conflict with meeting terms of the CZI award.
